items.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022
items.q: I’ll give you a couple of days off before if we can get this drummer from Texas” or something I don’t know. Paul Guerrera was his name, yeah, I remember.

ctx.x: Yeah recently I was trying to describe, okay when you’re playing for dancers you might start out with a two-beat, and then you get going, and then you go into swing. And they’re looking at me like what is this? Did you get to a point, you are a young man, did you ever think about the future? Like do I want to settle down? Am I looking for something that’s going to put me in one place like studio work etcetera?

Yeah well I met my wife and we got married in ’65. And that’s when I left Woody’s band. She’s fantastic. I mean she like, saves my life you know. And actually when we got married, I’ve got to tell you this story if you don’t mind, I told Woody I was going to get married. He goes, “You what? You’re what?” We’re sitting on a counter in a coffee shop. He says, “You’re getting married, what? Are you kidding?” I said, “Yeah, we’re getting married.” I said, “We’ve got to set a date” you know. And he says, “Oh, you…
He sure did. And for Frank.
